thread:
maria: Heads-up — metrics show a bunch of customers getting provisional > confirmed token diffs after stream reconnects + toolcall combos. Seen this in canary.
ryan: can you paste an example trace?
maria: yep — here’s a condensed session from the router logs (redacted):
```
SESSION_ID=abc123 route=eu-west-1 model=red-3 start=1610000000
-> stream start (client conn) tokens=0
-> toolcall invoked at seq=42, provisional_tokens=120
-> conn reset (client reconnect) at seq=43
-> router reassigns to new worker, resumes with suffix, provisional recorded again tokens=120
-> final confirmed ledger only shows one confirmed 120, but provisional shows 240 for session window
```
maria: result is console shows spike in provisional charges and customer noticed rough bill estimate error.
aj: hmm — is this specifically when the toolcall happens right before disconnect?
maria: yes, seems timing-critical: when a toolcall extends the response and the client reconnects during the extended window.
sophia: how are we currently deduping provisional entries? I thought ledger had idempotency key on toolcall id + session?
ryan: we use session_id + sequence window, but router split and new worker generate a fresh provisional record because shard ownership changed before confirm.
denis: so ownership handshake race. Worker A writes provisional, then dies; Worker B resumes and writes provisional again because it can't see A's broken heartbeat.
aj: telemetry question — do we have a reliable signal to tie these provisional dups to a route handoff vs legitimate multi-call?
maria: current signal is session_id + provisional_count, but not route-owner. Could enrich with worker_instance and provisional_uuid.
sophia: adding worker_instance will help debugging but we still need a reconciliation rule for accounting.
ryan: options: 1) server-side dedupe on provisional_uuid (requires single global index) 2) conservative approach — mark overlapping provisional windows as tentatively merged in UI and only count confirmed tokens in estimates 3) attribute provisional to first writer and discard subsequent provisionals if within grace window.
aj: (2) is low engineering cost but UX will still confuse customers if the console shows provisional spikes.
denis: (1) is ideal but cross-shard index is heavy and could add latency. We can async reconcile later but need realtime guard.
sophia: what about a heartbeat ownership TTL: when worker writes provisional it also sets ownership lease for seq range. If worker disappears, other worker must read-lease and detect previous provisional and decide to adopt vs merge.
ryan: that still needs a consistent store for leases (redis?) and careful failure modes.
maria: from product: customers mainly care about "estimated" vs "billed" clarity — can we add a small UI change: show provisional as two columns: "provisional written" and "provisional dedupable" with hover explaining route handoff cases?
aj: we can add tooltip quick, but we should also emit a telemetry metric 'provisional_dedupe_candidates' for dashboards and alerts.
sophia: agree — we need metric + event that tags session ids with worker_leases so we can query. Suggested event fields: session_id, seq_range, writer_worker, lease_ttl, provisional_uuid.
ryan: can we retro-fit logs to emit provisional_uuid? Some workers already emit a trace_id — we can map trace_id -> provisional_uuid in postprocess to backfill.
aj: note: backfilling in warehouse will be expensive; but we could only enable for canary customers for a week.
maria: rollouts: propose small change set: A) add provisional_uuid to write path (cheap), B) emit metering event (session_id, provisional_uuid, worker_id) asynchronously, C) console tooltip + new provisional_dedupe metric and alert. Then we can measure scope.
denis: do we need to change router sticky policy? Might reduce handoffs but could increase load imbalance.
ryan: probably not safe to change sticky in prod yet. We can tweak canary.
sophia: for reconciliation rules after we gather telemetry, implementation idea: when confirming tokens, check for earlier provisional_uuid(s) for same seq_range and only convert the earliest provisional to confirmed, reconcile others by marking as deduped in ledger.
aj: ledger change risk: must preserve audit trail for billing. We should mark deduped provisional rows but keep them for history and not count them in estimate.
maria: billing team FYI — customers saw estimated cost jump in console but invoice unaffected. We should add a banner explaining provisional spikes are ephemeral.
aj: Could we also throttled sampling to detect affected customers (e.g., 0.1% of sessions)?
ryan: yes — add a rollout flag to enable extra sampling and provisional_uuid emission for select orgs.
sophia: timeline? We can A) land telemetry + UI in 2 weeks for canary, B) collect data 2 weeks, C) design reconcile logic and small ledger change 1–2 sprints after.
denis: agree. I'll prototype lease-based guard but keep it behind a feature flag.
maria: action items: @ryan add provisional_uuid to metering write path (PR), @maj add provisional_dedupe metric + console tooltip (task), @denis prototype lease detection (experiment), @aj own sampling rollout list and alert thresholds.
maria: pinging @metering-bot to create an alert when provisional_dedupe_candidates > 20% for any org in a 1h window.
metering-bot: created alert: "provisional_dedupe_candidates_high" threshold 20% per-org 1h. Link: https://alerts.internal/prov-dedupe/552450
ryan: will open PR today with minimal provisional_uuid write and event emission.
maj: I'll sketch the tooltip copy and console mock.
sophia: keeping ledger changes auditable is critical. We'll draft schema for deduped flags.
maria: thanks team — let's sync in the eng-platform weekly to review canary data. :thumbsup:
